binding.question: Under the retained circular, when must an SFC-authorised fund be treated as a complex product for distribution? Distinguish mandatory classification, discretionary designation, exclusions and missing classification evidence.

extraction.text:
The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has observed that investment funds may, for asset allocation and yield enhancement purposes, gain exposure to private credit and private equity (collectively, private market assets) via: direct exposure through investments in bank or non-bank direct lending in the form of loans or equities to unlisted companies (direct exposure)1; or indirect exposures2 including through investments in business development companies (BDCs)3, collateralised loan obligations (CLOs)4 or financial derivative instruments5.

 

 
  This circular provides guidance to management companies of funds that are authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong (Funds)6 in this regard. Funds with direct or indirect exposure to private market assets are required to observe the enhanced disclosure requirements set out in this circular. A Fund may be subject to enhanced scrutiny by the SFC in some cases and be classified as a complex product for distribution, where appropriate.

 

 
  Direct investment in private market assets generally carries higher inherent risks than publicly listed securities, as these assets are typically illiquid, hard to value, and subject to limited regulatory oversight; they also have higher credit risks and thus higher risk of default. While indirect exposures to the private market assets may not present the same level of risk as direct investments, recent market developments have raised concerns about these indirect exposures, such as the rising default risks of underlying investments for private credit funds, widening price-to-NAV discount for listed BDCs, etc. In addition, certain indirect exposures may lack transparency about the underlying private market assets, as they involve layered structures or complex financial instruments such that retail investors may not reasonably understand the features and risks of these indirect exposures.

 

 
  Considering that retail investors in Hong Kong may have limited familiarity with private market assets and their associated risks, fund managers should ensure that investors are provided with a clear, sufficiently complete and balanced picture of the characteristics, nature and extent of risks associated with various types of exposures a Fund may have to private market assets. Fund managers should also, among other things, ensure that the distributors chosen are appropriate for covering the target market of their Funds.

  Enhanced disclosure in offering documents

 

 
  If a Fund may have direct or indirect exposure to private market assets, its fund manager should ensure that the Fund’s offering document (including the key facts statement (KFS)) clearly discloses:

  (i)        the extent and the means of access of exposure (eg, up to [x]% of the Fund’s NAV is invested in listed BDCs which primarily invest in private market assets; [x – y%] of the Fund’s NAV will gain exposure to private loans via investment in senior tranche of CLOs);

  (ii)       the nature and characteristics of the underlying private market assets (eg, the minimum credit rating of the CLOs in which the Fund invests, TRSs on an index comprising unsecuritised broadly syndicated loans); and

  (iii)      in the offering documents (and where appropriate, the KFS), the key risks associated with the Fund’s exposure to the specific types of private market assets it directly or indirectly invests in, including the impact and implications to the Fund and its investors (e.g. the limited liquidity and lack of transparency of the underlying private market assets of the BDCs can make them more challenging to value, and these valuation uncertainties may negatively impact the BDC’s NAV and hence the Fund’s NAV).

  Complex product designation

 

 
  A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV. On a case-by-case basis, the SFC may also designate a Fund as a complex product, taking into account factors including, without limitation:

  •        the aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets of the Fund;
   
   •        the Fund's overall investment strategy, portfolio composition, and liquidity and/or risk profile;
   
   •        the extent, nature and characteristics of the specific asset types in which the Fund invests (eg, the tranches and credit ratings of CLOs; the structure, tranches and underlying assets of SRTs); and
   
   •        any distribution restrictions, requirements or other conditions as may be imposed by the Fund’s home regulators.

  In assessing whether the complex product designation is warranted7, the SFC will adopt a holistic approach taking into account the specific circumstances of the case.

 

 
  A Fund classified as a complex product will be subject to the SFC’s prevailing requirements for the sale of complex products8 including but not limited to ensuring the suitability of the Fund for its investors irrespective of whether solicitation or recommendation is involved.

  Target market identification and distributor selection

 

 
  The SFC wishes to remind fund managers to observe the requirements set out in the “Circular to Product Providers of SFC-authorized unit trusts and mutual funds, SFC-authorized investment-linked assurance schemes and SFC-authorized unlisted structured investment products – Guidance on Internal Product Approval Process”9, which outlines, among others, the requirements regarding target market identification and distributor selection for SFC-authorised funds.

 

 
  Fund managers should carefully identify the target market to ensure that the Fund, including its underlying investments and associated risks, would be generally understood by the target market and that the Fund’s investment objectives and risk/return profile match the needs and risk appetite of the target market. They should also ensure that the distributors chosen are appropriate for covering the target market identified, have the necessary product knowledge to understand the Fund (including whether the Fund is a complex product) and to assign an appropriate product risk rating (if applicable) for the Fund, and advise investors accordingly.

 

 
  Fund managers are further reminded that the marketing materials of SFC-authorised funds must comply with the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes10, which provide, among other requirements, that advertisements of a Fund should be fair and present a balanced picture of the Fund with adequate risk disclosures.

  Others

 

 
  When seeking the SFC’s authorisation for any new funds that may have direct or indirect exposure to private market assets, the fund may be subject to the SFC’s closer scrutiny. In some cases, the SFC may not process the fund under the Fund Authorisation Simple Track (FASTrack).

 

 
  For existing SFC-authorised funds that may have direct or indirect exposure to private market assets, fund managers are expected to undertake a review of their funds, take appropriate actions including updating the Fund’s offering documents as soon as practicable, and ensure necessary and proper communications with the distributors in light of the guidance provided under this circular (in particular, with respect to paragraphs 9 and 10 above). Fund managers are encouraged to consult the SFC at the earliest opportunity if they are in doubt regarding complex product classification of their Funds.

 

 
  If you wish to seek clarification of any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.

   

 




 Investment Products Division 
        Securities and Futures Commission

  



 1 Direct investments in/exposures to private assets fall within the investment limit of 15% of a Fund’s total net asset value (NAV) under 7.3 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds (UT Code).



 2 The examples of indirect exposures set out in paragraph 1 above are non-exhaustive, and subject to review and update by the SFC from time to time in view of market developments.



 3 BDCs are close-ended funds registered under the US Investment Company Act of 1940, which primarily invest in debt and equity of small and mid-sized companies in the US.



 4 CLOs are securities backed by a pool of debt, typically leveraged loans and broadly syndicated loans, or direct lending to unlisted companies.



 5 For example, Total Return Swaps on indices with exposure to leveraged loans or broadly syndicated loans (TRSs), or Significant Risk Transfers with underlying assets that are corporate loans (SRTs).



 6 Except for listed closed-ended alternative asset funds (LAFs). For LAFs, please refer to the circular on LAFs: https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/circular/products/product-authorization/doc?refNo=25EC9

 7 In cases where the Fund’s aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets are less than 50% of the Fund’s NAV.



 8 Paragraph 5.5 of the SFC’s Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission and Chapter 6 of the SFC’s Guidelines on Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms, and the relevant Frequently Asked Questions.



 9 Issued by the SFC on 30 April 2014 and subsequently updated on 4 March 2016. Please refer to: https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/circular/products/product-authorization/doc?refNo=16EC11



 10 Latest version issued by the SFC in April 2013. classification_assumptions: The assessment concerns one SFC-authorised fund offered to the public in Hong Kong; listed closed-ended alternative asset funds are excluded from this circular's scope.

Direct exposure, indirect exposure and NAV are measured at the same assessment time in a common exact valuation unit. Integer inputs require an exact common scale, without rounding at the 50% boundary.
The supplied exposure amounts use an established measurement and aggregation method that avoids unintended double counting. The retained text does not establish that method.
An SFC designation means an actual designation applicable to this Fund at the assessment time; risk factors or enhanced scrutiny alone do not establish designation.
The result addresses classification under this circular, not overall distribution compliance or classification under other instruments.

reading.distinction: The model separates the Fund from its underlying assets and intermediate instruments, adds direct and indirect exposure, and distinguishes an automatic threshold from an actual discretionary SFC decision. Neither below-threshold exposure nor missing designation evidence establishes non-complex status. LAF exclusion is a scope exclusion, not a finding that the fund is non-complex. The separate 15% direct-investment limit is not this classification threshold.

reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] For an in-scope Fund with positive NAV, does either classification route under this circular require treating the Fund as a complex product for distribution at the assessment time? True means total direct and indirect private-market exposure is at least 50% of NAV, or an applicable SFC designation exists. False means exposure is below 50% and no applicable designation exists; it does not establish non-complex status under other rules or prevent future designation. Missing facts remain unknown, and an out-of-scope fund receives no classification answer. This is a classification predicate, not legal approval or a compliance finding.

citations.quote: This circular provides guidance to management companies of funds that are authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong (Funds)6 in this regard.

A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV. On a case-by-case basis, the SFC may also designate a Fund as a complex product, taking into account factors including, without limitation:
In assessing whether the complex product designation is warranted7, the SFC will adopt a holistic approach taking into account the specific circumstances of the case.
In cases where the Fund’s aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets are less than 50% of the Fund’s NAV.
Except for listed closed-ended alternative asset funds (LAFs).
The examples of indirect exposures set out in paragraph 1 above are non-exhaustive, and subject to review and update by the SFC from time to time in view of market developments.

A Fund classified as a complex product will be subject to the SFC’s prevailing requirements for the sale of complex products8 including but not limited to ensuring the suitability of the Fund for its investors irrespective of whether solicitation or recommendation is involved.

reading.distinction: Inspection of both prior models found that they already distinguish the relevant actors, underlying assets, intermediate instruments, fund-wide aggregation, exclusions and operative designation. No source-supported rival threshold rule was identified. The consequential remaining distinction is between a contemporaneous classification basis and an enduring classification status: a below-threshold snapshot without an operative designation does not resolve the effect of an earlier threshold crossing. Missing evidence also differs from evidence that a classification basis is absent. The proposal therefore retains the two classification routes while expressly limiting the question answered.

reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Does an in-scope Fund have a contemporaneous complex-product classification basis under this circular? True means aggregate direct and indirect private-market exposure is at least 50% of NAV or an operative SFC designation exists, requiring complex-product treatment on that basis. False means both bases are absent on established facts; it does not establish declassification following an earlier threshold crossing or non-complex status under other rules. assumptions: CONDITIONAL proposal only. These bindings do not approve semantic equivalence.
Both controls concern the same fund, assessment occasion and applicable circular. Commencement and the governing assessment date are not established by this packet.

Both original outputs explicitly use TRUE_IS_SATISFIED: true denotes satisfaction of a classification trigger, not prohibition or compliance. The required output enum cannot express that convention. The two TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT entries below are schema-only placeholders, not semantic bindings; this proposal is blocked from operative use unless the schema supports TRUE_IS_SATISFIED. No source-supported conversion to either permitted output convention is established.

Common facts are Boolean propositions with separately preserved evidence states: established true, established false, unknown or conflicting. Unknown and conflicting evidence must not be coerced into Boolean values or silently resolved by a binding.

Bindings are conditional on matching evidence, asset definitions, assessment basis and timing on both sides. Disagreement in those matters remains unresolved rather than being erased by common fact names.

The exposure fact requires a supported common methodology for total direct and indirect exposure and NAV. The packet does not establish a complete measurement protocol; illustrative holdings, permitted exposure and disclosure examples cannot supply one.
Private market assets means private credit and private equity. The listed forms of indirect exposure are non-exhaustive.

An operative designation requires evidence of an actual SFC decision applicable at the assessment occasion. Possible designation, adverse risk factors, consultation, scrutiny and missing records neither establish nor negate a designation. Continued designation or declassification after an exposure change is not settled here.

Both scopes derive as (and common_public_sfc_authorised (not common_is_laf)). Established false scope yields no classification decision under this control, not a false classification result. Unresolved or conflicting scope must remain flagged.

For established in-scope funds, both proposed results derive as (or common_exposure_at_least_50_percent common_operative_sfc_designation). An established true route can determine satisfaction despite an unknown other route; false requires both routes established false. Conflicting evidence remains explicitly flagged and cannot be represented as an uncontested Boolean determination.
Classification does not establish compliance with resulting sale requirements, general non-complex status, or treatment under excluded or missing instruments.

findings.question: No prior models were supplied for challenger inspection. The proposal addresses consequential omissions of intermediate instruments, aggregate exposure, the SFC as decision-maker, LAF exclusion and assessment timing; the evidence does not justify a rival threshold rule.

The SFC's prospective discretionary judgment cannot be computed from the retained non-exhaustive factors in this expression fragment. The model records an actual decision rather than predicting whether the SFC ought to designate a Fund.
The three source dependencies have no supplied content. The LAF regime and the full prevailing complex-product distribution requirements cannot be reconstructed from their references.

If an exact common exposure scale or a defensible aggregation methodology cannot be established, the numerical classification route remains unevaluable; rounded percentages must not silently decide the boundary.

No prior models were supplied for comparison. The present model explicitly separates underlying assets, intermediary instruments, aggregate exposure, SFC designation and its timing; the retained evidence does not require a rival threshold interpretation.

The SFC’s holistic discretion cannot be derived as an automatic Boolean decision from its non-exhaustive factors. Strategy, portfolio, liquidity, risk, instrument characteristics and home-regulator conditions inform discretion but supply no deterministic weighting or cutoff.
The three missing dependencies have no supplied substantive text. Their effects, and any additional classification routes under referenced instruments, remain unresolved.

The formula requires exact commensurable integer measurements and positive NAV. If those prerequisites cannot be established, this formalization cannot decide the threshold; no rounding or zero-NAV rule is inferred.

Both supplied prior models were inspected. No consequential rival based on omitted actors, components or aggregation quantifiers is supported by the retained text; a second proposal would manufacture ambiguity.
The retained source supplies no rule determining whether classification persists after exposure falls below 50%. A historical-status model cannot be completed without that rule.
The SFC's prospective holistic judgment cannot be computed from the non-exhaustive factors using this expression fragment; an actual designation must be established separately.
Exposure measurement and the content of missing dependencies remain unresolved. Neither the prior models nor this proposal establishes legal completeness.
Can all amounts be represented exactly on a common integer scale, and does the evaluator use arithmetic without overflow or boundary-changing rounding?

For prem.core.application, what establishes the circular's applicability and the governing assessment occasion? Document-update timing does not itself establish commencement or a classification grace period.
For prem.core.laf, what establishes the assessed Fund's own LAF status, independently of its investments? The separate LAF circular is absent.
For prem.scope.measurement and the numerical domain assumptions, what authority governs current versus permitted exposure, look-through, derivatives, netting, overlap and valuation dates?

For prem.time.limited_target, is the intended operational question only whether current routes are satisfied, or the Fund's continuing classification status? What authority resolves prior threshold crossings and subsequent declines?
How does the evaluator represent unknown facts separately from false facts and out-of-scope results? The displayed Boolean expressions alone do not specify partial-information semantics.

No substantive conflict among the eight limited two-route readings warrants an attack or overall preference on this packet. Their remaining differences concern abstraction, computational domain and temporal scope; none establishes an exhaustive legal-status decision.

The source does not specify exposure aggregation, derivative measurement, look-through, netting or treatment of temporary threshold crossings.

residual_questions.question: No prior models were supplied for challenger inspection. The proposal addresses consequential omissions of intermediate instruments, aggregate exposure, the SFC as decision-maker, LAF exclusion and assessment timing; the evidence does not justify a rival threshold rule.

The SFC's prospective discretionary judgment cannot be computed from the retained non-exhaustive factors in this expression fragment. The model records an actual decision rather than predicting whether the SFC ought to designate a Fund.
The three source dependencies have no supplied content. The LAF regime and the full prevailing complex-product distribution requirements cannot be reconstructed from their references.

If an exact common exposure scale or a defensible aggregation methodology cannot be established, the numerical classification route remains unevaluable; rounded percentages must not silently decide the boundary.

No prior models were supplied for comparison. The present model explicitly separates underlying assets, intermediary instruments, aggregate exposure, SFC designation and its timing; the retained evidence does not require a rival threshold interpretation.

The SFC’s holistic discretion cannot be derived as an automatic Boolean decision from its non-exhaustive factors. Strategy, portfolio, liquidity, risk, instrument characteristics and home-regulator conditions inform discretion but supply no deterministic weighting or cutoff.
The three missing dependencies have no supplied substantive text. Their effects, and any additional classification routes under referenced instruments, remain unresolved.

The formula requires exact commensurable integer measurements and positive NAV. If those prerequisites cannot be established, this formalization cannot decide the threshold; no rounding or zero-NAV rule is inferred.

Both supplied prior models were inspected. No consequential rival based on omitted actors, components or aggregation quantifiers is supported by the retained text; a second proposal would manufacture ambiguity.
The retained source supplies no rule determining whether classification persists after exposure falls below 50%. A historical-status model cannot be completed without that rule.
The SFC's prospective holistic judgment cannot be computed from the non-exhaustive factors using this expression fragment; an actual designation must be established separately.
Exposure measurement and the content of missing dependencies remain unresolved. Neither the prior models nor this proposal establishes legal completeness.
Can all amounts be represented exactly on a common integer scale, and does the evaluator use arithmetic without overflow or boundary-changing rounding?

For prem.core.application, what establishes the circular's applicability and the governing assessment occasion? Document-update timing does not itself establish commencement or a classification grace period.
For prem.core.laf, what establishes the assessed Fund's own LAF status, independently of its investments? The separate LAF circular is absent.
For prem.scope.measurement and the numerical domain assumptions, what authority governs current versus permitted exposure, look-through, derivatives, netting, overlap and valuation dates?

For prem.time.limited_target, is the intended operational question only whether current routes are satisfied, or the Fund's continuing classification status? What authority resolves prior threshold crossings and subsequent declines?
How does the evaluator represent unknown facts separately from false facts and out-of-scope results? The displayed Boolean expressions alone do not specify partial-information semantics.

No substantive conflict among the eight limited two-route readings warrants an attack or overall preference on this packet. Their remaining differences concern abstraction, computational domain and temporal scope; none establishes an exhaustive legal-status decision.

additional_concerns: The discretionary-factor omissions identify limits of executable coverage, not necessarily code defects. A formula consuming an evidenced SFC designation need not reproduce the regulator's deliberation. It must not be presented as independently deciding whether designation is warranted.

Footnote 7 qualifies the holistic designation assessment as concerning exposure below 50% of NAV. The representation does not encode that qualification within designation assessment. Its disjunction is nevertheless compatible with the two classification routes: exposure at or above 50% already suffices. The source does not establish that a previously operative designation ceases upon a threshold crossing, so adding a current below-50% guard could introduce an unsupported restriction.

The factor list also includes home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements and conditions in d4148dd852cee.u28.4505. Neither that factor nor the holistic, non-exhaustive assessment is executable here. If the candidate were expanded to generate designation decisions, implementing only the factors covered by the required pairs would be incomplete.

The aggregate input refers to 'the applicable methodology', but the supplied source does not specify a calculation procedure for indirect exposure, look-through, valuation timing or avoidance of double counting. Missing measurement evidence is correctly kept unresolved in the input description; no particular methodology has been validated. Any additional authority needed to establish that methodology is unidentified and must not be assigned an invented dependency ID.

The mandatory trigger concerns total direct and indirect exposure. Footnote 1's 15% direct-investment limit does not replace the 50% aggregate threshold or establish that the latter is unreachable. UT Code 7.3 is not supplied; it would be needed to reconstruct the separate investment-limit regime, not to establish the narrow classification trigger.

The LAF exclusion is stated directly in footnote 6 and appears in scope. The separate LAF circular is not supplied, and is_laf remains a judgment input. Assessing an ambiguous fund's LAF status or its separate regulatory treatment may require that authority; the packet provides no identifiable dependency mapping for it. Exclusion here does not establish non-complex status under another regime.

The runtime rule that any conflicting fact blocks evaluation even on an unselected branch is an added evidentiary policy, not a requirement stated by the circular. It can withhold a result when one classification route is otherwise established. Distinguish an evaluator's refusal to resolve conflicting records from the legal sufficiency of an established trigger.

The question's false_means phrase 'neither ... is established' could be read as mere absence of evidence. The representation instead requires known false inputs for an in-scope FALSE result and preserves missing evidence as UNKNOWN. Keep that distinction explicit; missing designation records do not establish absence of designation.

The consultation claim's OBLIGATION/SHOULD metadata is stronger than the source's 'encouraged' wording if treated as mandatory. Its prose statement preserves the source qualification. Consultation must not be added as a prerequisite to classification or as permission to treat uncertainty as non-complex status.

No supplied external dependency has a non-null source_hash, and the three unbound IDs are not mapped to named authorities. None can be marked AVAILABLE. The missing sales authorities remain unresolved even though their downstream requirements are outside this typed question.

The packet supports the retained circular's propositions, not an independently verified statement of current law. The source does not establish that an existing designation ceases when exposure crosses the threshold; adding a current below-50% guard to operative_sfc_designation could impose an unsupported restriction.

The non-exhaustive designation factors also include home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements and conditions in d4148dd852cee.u28.4505. Any extension that generates designation decisions would need to account for that factor and the holistic assessment, without converting individual factors into automatic triggers. Applicable home-regulator measures would require separate evidence if used; none is identified here.

The aggregate input's 'applicable methodology' is not a supplied calculation procedure. Look-through, derivative exposure measurement, valuation timing and avoidance of double counting remain unimplemented and unvalidated. Which additional authority, if any, is necessary to settle those choices is uncertain; no dependency ID can be assigned. Before operational use, identify the methodology and its evidentiary or authoritative basis.

The 15% direct-investment limit in footnote 1 does not replace the 50% total direct-and-indirect classification threshold. UT Code 7.3 is missing and would be needed to reconstruct the separate investment-limit regime. Its absence does not prevent source support for the narrow classification trigger.

The LAF exclusion is directly supported and represented in scope. The separate LAF circular identified by footnote 6 is missing. It may be required to resolve disputed LAF status or separate regulatory treatment; no supplied dependency mapping identifies it. OUT_OF_SCOPE must not imply non-complex status under another regime.

The runtime provision 'A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch.' adds an evidence-handling restriction not stated by the circular. It can withhold a result despite an otherwise established sufficient route, or despite a scope fact that would otherwise settle exclusion. This is an operational refusal to evaluate, not an additional legal classification condition.

The question's false_means wording 'neither aggregate exposure of at least 50% of NAV nor an operative SFC designation is established' risks confusing lack of evidence with established absence. Within known scope, the representation requires both route inputs to be FALSE for FALSE; missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless another established route determines TRUE.

Consultation is encouraged, and product risk rating is qualified by 'if applicable'. Neither may be converted into a mandatory classification prerequisite. Conversely, consultation or unresolved measurement does not grant permission to treat a Fund as non-complex.

All three supplied external dependency records have null source_hash values and no identifying mappings. None qualifies as AVAILABLE, and none can reliably be assigned to a named missing authority. Source unit IDs are not dependency IDs.

The Internal Product Approval Process circular identified in d4148dd852cee.u36.5149 and footnote 9, and the Advertising Guidelines identified in d4148dd852cee.u42.6275 and footnote 10, are also absent. They would be necessary to reconstruct those broader incorporated regimes, but are not needed for the narrow distributor statements or classification output assessed here.

additional_concerns: The discretionary-factor omissions identify limits of executable coverage, not necessarily code defects. A formula consuming an evidenced SFC designation need not reproduce the regulator's deliberation. It must not be presented as independently deciding whether designation is warranted.

Footnote 7 qualifies the holistic designation assessment as concerning exposure below 50% of NAV. The representation does not encode that qualification within designation assessment. Its disjunction is nevertheless compatible with the two classification routes: exposure at or above 50% already suffices. The source does not establish that a previously operative designation ceases upon a threshold crossing, so adding a current below-50% guard could introduce an unsupported restriction.

The factor list also includes home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements and conditions in d4148dd852cee.u28.4505. Neither that factor nor the holistic, non-exhaustive assessment is executable here. If the candidate were expanded to generate designation decisions, implementing only the factors covered by the required pairs would be incomplete.

The aggregate input refers to 'the applicable methodology', but the supplied source does not specify a calculation procedure for indirect exposure, look-through, valuation timing or avoidance of double counting. Missing measurement evidence is correctly kept unresolved in the input description; no particular methodology has been validated. Any additional authority needed to establish that methodology is unidentified and must not be assigned an invented dependency ID.

The mandatory trigger concerns total direct and indirect exposure. Footnote 1's 15% direct-investment limit does not replace the 50% aggregate threshold or establish that the latter is unreachable. UT Code 7.3 is not supplied; it would be needed to reconstruct the separate investment-limit regime, not to establish the narrow classification trigger.

The LAF exclusion is stated directly in footnote 6 and appears in scope. The separate LAF circular is not supplied, and is_laf remains a judgment input. Assessing an ambiguous fund's LAF status or its separate regulatory treatment may require that authority; the packet provides no identifiable dependency mapping for it. Exclusion here does not establish non-complex status under another regime.

The runtime rule that any conflicting fact blocks evaluation even on an unselected branch is an added evidentiary policy, not a requirement stated by the circular. It can withhold a result when one classification route is otherwise established. Distinguish an evaluator's refusal to resolve conflicting records from the legal sufficiency of an established trigger.

The question's false_means phrase 'neither ... is established' could be read as mere absence of evidence. The representation instead requires known false inputs for an in-scope FALSE result and preserves missing evidence as UNKNOWN. Keep that distinction explicit; missing designation records do not establish absence of designation.

The consultation claim's OBLIGATION/SHOULD metadata is stronger than the source's 'encouraged' wording if treated as mandatory. Its prose statement preserves the source qualification. Consultation must not be added as a prerequisite to classification or as permission to treat uncertainty as non-complex status.

No supplied external dependency has a non-null source_hash, and the three unbound IDs are not mapped to named authorities. None can be marked AVAILABLE. The missing sales authorities remain unresolved even though their downstream requirements are outside this typed question.

The packet supports the retained circular's propositions, not an independently verified statement of current law. No actual assessment date, portfolio evidence or designation record is supplied, so these checks establish neither a particular Fund's classification nor compliance with downstream duties.

additional_concerns: OMITS identifies unimplemented upstream assessments, not necessarily defects relative to the exact typed question. A formula consuming an evidenced designation need not reproduce the SFC's deliberation. It must not be presented as independently determining whether designation is warranted. No prior dispute is resolved merely by repeating a label.

Footnote 7 places the holistic designation assessment below 50% of NAV. The disjunction does not encode that qualification, but exposure at or above 50% already suffices. The source does not establish that an existing designation ceases when exposure crosses the threshold; adding a current below-50% guard to operative_sfc_designation could impose an unsupported restriction.

The non-exhaustive designation factors also include home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements and conditions in d4148dd852cee.u28.4505. Any extension that generates designation decisions would need to account for that factor and the holistic assessment, without converting individual factors into automatic triggers. Applicable home-regulator measures would require separate evidence if used; none is identified here.

The aggregate input's 'applicable methodology' is not a supplied calculation procedure. Look-through, derivative exposure measurement, valuation timing and avoidance of double counting remain unimplemented and unvalidated. Which additional authority, if any, is necessary to settle those choices is uncertain; no dependency ID can be assigned. Before operational use, identify the methodology and its evidentiary or authoritative basis.

The 15% direct-investment limit in footnote 1 does not replace the 50% total direct-and-indirect classification threshold. UT Code 7.3 is missing and would be needed to reconstruct the separate investment-limit regime. Its absence does not prevent source support for the narrow classification trigger.

The LAF exclusion is directly supported and represented in scope. The separate LAF circular identified by footnote 6 is missing. It may be required to resolve disputed LAF status or separate regulatory treatment; no supplied dependency mapping identifies it. OUT_OF_SCOPE must not imply non-complex status under another regime.

The runtime provision 'A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch.' adds an evidence-handling restriction not stated by the circular. It can withhold a result despite an otherwise established sufficient route, or despite a scope fact that would otherwise settle exclusion. This is an operational refusal to evaluate, not an additional legal classification condition.

The question's false_means wording 'neither aggregate exposure of at least 50% of NAV nor an operative SFC designation is established' risks confusing lack of evidence with established absence. Within known scope, the representation requires both route inputs to be FALSE for FALSE; missing evidence remains UNKNOWN unless another established route determines TRUE.

Consultation is encouraged, and product risk rating is qualified by 'if applicable'. Neither may be converted into a mandatory classification prerequisite. Conversely, consultation or unresolved measurement does not grant permission to treat a Fund as non-complex.

All three supplied external dependency records have null source_hash values and no identifying mappings. None qualifies as AVAILABLE, and none can reliably be assigned to a named missing authority. Source unit IDs are not dependency IDs.

The Internal Product Approval Process circular identified in d4148dd852cee.u36.5149 and footnote 9, and the Advertising Guidelines identified in d4148dd852cee.u42.6275 and footnote 10, are also absent. They would be necessary to reconstruct those broader incorporated regimes, but are not needed for the narrow distributor statements or classification output assessed here.

The supported BDC claims concern the circular's description. Independent verification under the US Investment Company Act of 1940 would require additional authority and is not established by this packet. Likewise, the possibility of later SFC updates does not prove that updates exist or apply.

These checks assess the retained source and supplied representation. They do not establish current law, an actual Fund's classification, the correctness of supplied judgment inputs, or downstream compliance. No assessment date, portfolio measurements or designation records have been provided. No unsupported additional numerical threshold, categorical exclusion or affirmative permission is visible in the Boolean formula.

MISSING would describe application to a particular Fund if the authority field also encompasses the absent designation decision. additional_concerns: The exact runtime restriction is: "A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch." This is an implementation policy, not a condition stated in the circular. It can withhold a result when scope and one independently sufficient classification route are established but another fact conflicts. This does not authorize a negative classification; its interaction with route sufficiency needs separate review.

The inclusive automatic trigger is locally supported by: "A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV." The representation's Boolean exposure input does not implement valuation, aggregation, indirect-exposure measurement or asset identification. Actual Fund classification remains unestablished without those inputs.

The definition and derivative examples receive OMITS only for their absence from the represented upstream assessment. A correctly supplied Boolean exposure fact could still make the classification formula faithful. Conversely, merely naming the input does not establish that the definition or examples were applied correctly.

The discretionary-factor PRESERVES proposals are limited to the exact question about an actual classification basis. The representation preserves the need for an actual applicable designation, but omits the SFC's factor-by-factor assessment. If the intended task were to decide whether designation is warranted, this formula would not implement that task.

The source also lists asset-specific characteristics and home-regulator conditions as discretionary considerations, and says the list is non-exhaustive. Neither those considerations nor the two checked factors may be converted into automatic designation rules or a closed checklist.

The retained text supplies no effective-date rule, classification grace period, designation persistence rule or withdrawal procedure. The single-assessment-time convention requires supporting evidence of temporal applicability; document-update timing does not supply that evidence.
No supplied dependency has a non-null source_hash, and the three unbound dependency IDs have no identifiable authority mappings. No AVAILABLE assessment or invented catalogue match is justified.

Additional referenced authorities absent from the packet include the separate LAF circular, the Guidance on Internal Product Approval Process circular and the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes. Their absence does not prevent assessing the local classification trigger; their contents would be needed for separate claims about those regimes.

FALSE means neither route is established as true only when the necessary negative facts are established within known scope. An unsearched designation history, missing holdings or unresolved measurement cannot supply those negative facts. OUT_OF_SCOPE for LAFs and FALSE for an in-scope Fund do not establish permission to sell, overall compliance or non-complex status under other authorities.

additional_concerns: The exact runtime restriction is: "A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch." This is an implementation policy, not a condition stated in the circular. It can withhold a result when scope and one independently sufficient classification route are established but another fact conflicts. This does not authorize a negative classification; its interaction with route sufficiency needs separate review.

The inclusive automatic trigger is locally supported by: "A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV." The representation's Boolean exposure input does not implement valuation, aggregation, indirect-exposure measurement or asset identification. Actual Fund classification remains unestablished without those inputs.

The definition and derivative examples receive OMITS only for their absence from the represented upstream assessment. A correctly supplied Boolean exposure fact could still make the classification formula faithful. Conversely, merely naming the input does not establish that the definition or examples were applied correctly.

The discretionary-factor PRESERVES proposals are limited to the exact question about an actual classification basis. The representation preserves the need for an actual applicable designation, but omits the SFC's factor-by-factor assessment. If the intended task were to decide whether designation is warranted, this formula would not implement that task.

The source also lists asset-specific characteristics and home-regulator conditions as discretionary considerations, and says the list is non-exhaustive. Neither those considerations nor the two checked factors may be converted into automatic designation rules or a closed checklist.

The retained text supplies no effective-date rule, classification grace period, designation persistence rule or withdrawal procedure. The single-assessment-time convention requires supporting evidence of temporal applicability; document-update timing does not supply that evidence.
No supplied dependency has a non-null source_hash, and the three unbound dependency IDs have no identifiable authority mappings. No AVAILABLE assessment or invented catalogue match is justified.

Additional referenced authorities absent from the packet include the separate LAF circular, the Guidance on Internal Product Approval Process circular and the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes. Their absence does not prevent assessing the local classification trigger; their contents would be needed for separate claims about those regimes.

FALSE means neither route is established as true only when the necessary negative facts are established within known scope. An unsearched designation history, missing holdings or unresolved measurement cannot supply those negative facts. OUT_OF_SCOPE for LAFs and FALSE for an in-scope Fund do not establish permission to sell, overall compliance or non-complex status under other authorities.

All twelve required pairs are retained. These scoped proposals do not resolve the prior disputes by consensus, certify the complete implementation or authorize pruning claims outside this typed question.

additional_concerns: These assessments concern the supplied source and declared representation. No Fund-specific evidence, executable implementation or runtime results are supplied; the labels do not establish a classification for any actual Fund.

Footnote 7 expressly places the holistic discretionary assessment below 50% of NAV. The representation does not expressly guard the designation branch with a below-threshold condition. For consistent known Boolean inputs, threshold OR designation and threshold OR (NOT threshold AND designation) give the same classification result. Thus the missing guard is a source-context omission, not an established output defect; it must not imply that the automatic route requires a separate SFC decision.

The global conflict rule blocks evaluation even when an independently established route would suffice. For example, a conflict about designation can block a known at-least-50% threshold result. This is an additional evidentiary restriction imposed by the runtime, not a condition stated by the circular. Whether it is an intended operational safeguard remains unresolved.

The circular does not supply exposure measurement, look-through, valuation, netting or aggregation methods in the retained text. The representation acknowledges that these are unresolved input judgments. If applying the rule requires further measurement authority, that authority is missing and must be identified; no supplied dependency ID can presently be matched to it.

An assessment relying on the discretionary route needs the actual Fund-specific SFC designation and evidence of its temporal applicability. Those materials are not supplied. A false designation input likewise requires adequate evidence; an unsearched history cannot establish absence. No identifiable dependency ID for such materials is provided.

The supplied text does not establish effective dates, designation persistence or later amendments. Applying this rule at a particular time requires those matters to be resolved where material. The mere possibility of later updates does not establish that an update exists.

The three supplied external dependency IDs all have null source_hash values and no descriptions identifying their authorities. None can be marked AVAILABLE or reliably assigned to a particular missing authority. All pair-level NONE_DECLARED assessments concern support for the narrow claims, not completeness of evidence for a Fund-specific determination.

Additional external authorities expressly referenced by the retained source but not supplied with identifiable mappings are UT Code section 7.3; the LAF circular refNo=25EC9; Code of Conduct paragraph 5.5; Chapter 6 of the Guidelines on Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms and relevant FAQs; the internal product-approval circular refNo=16EC11; and the cited advertising guidelines. Their absence does not defeat claims stated directly in this circular, but it prevents assessment of their full incorporated requirements.

Footnote 1 states a 15% limit on direct private-asset investments or exposures under UT Code section 7.3. That separate investment restriction must not be substituted for the 50% aggregate classification threshold, used to cap observed exposure artificially, or treated as permission for all exposures below 50%. Overall investment-limit compliance is outside this question.

Footnote 6 excludes a category of assessed Funds. It does not exclude every listed closed-ended holding from indirect exposure. In particular, the BDC description must not be conflated with the LAF exclusion.

The factors also include home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements or conditions under unit d4148dd852cee.u28.4505. These are not represented as executable factor assessments. Like the listed asset and Fund characteristics, they inform SFC discretion and do not themselves substitute for an actual designation.

The consultation statement is supported as encouragement. Its OBLIGATION/SHOULD metadata would overstate the source if a downstream process treated it as a mandatory consultation condition or an independent classification trigger.

A false classification result does not establish overall compliance, permission to distribute without other requirements, or absence of classification under another regime. OUT_OF_SCOPE for a LAF likewise does not establish that the Fund is non-complex under its separate regime.

The discretionary-factor and definition omissions are upstream assessment boundaries, not automatic instructions to add predicates to the Boolean rule. Their proper treatment depends on whether a separate, adequately supported input-assessment process exists.

Footnote 7 expressly places the holistic discretionary assessment below 50% of NAV. The representation does not expressly guard the designation branch with a below-threshold condition. For consistent known Boolean inputs, threshold OR designation and threshold OR (NOT threshold AND designation) give the same classification result. Thus the missing guard is a source-context omission, not an established output defect; it must not imply that the automatic route requires a separate SFC decision.

The global conflict rule blocks evaluation even when an independently established route would suffice. For example, a conflict about designation can block a known at-least-50% threshold result. This is an additional evidentiary restriction imposed by the runtime, not a condition stated by the circular. Whether it is an intended operational safeguard remains unresolved.

The circular does not supply exposure measurement, look-through, valuation, netting or aggregation methods in the retained text. The representation acknowledges that these are unresolved input judgments. If applying the rule requires further measurement authority, that authority is missing and must be identified; no supplied dependency ID can presently be matched to it.

An assessment relying on the discretionary route needs the actual Fund-specific SFC designation and evidence of its temporal applicability. Those materials are not supplied. A false designation input likewise requires adequate evidence; an unsearched history cannot establish absence. No identifiable dependency ID for such materials is provided.

The supplied text does not establish effective dates, designation persistence or later amendments. Applying this rule at a particular time requires those matters to be resolved where material. The mere possibility of later updates does not establish that an update exists.

The three supplied external dependency IDs all have null source_hash values and no descriptions identifying their authorities. None can be marked AVAILABLE or reliably assigned to a particular missing authority. All pair-level NONE_DECLARED assessments concern support for the narrow claims, not completeness of evidence for a Fund-specific determination.

Additional external authorities expressly referenced by the retained source but not supplied with identifiable mappings are UT Code section 7.3; the LAF circular refNo=25EC9; Code of Conduct paragraph 5.5; Chapter 6 of the Guidelines on Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms and relevant FAQs; the internal product-approval circular refNo=16EC11; and the cited advertising guidelines. Their absence does not defeat claims stated directly in this circular, but it prevents assessment of their full incorporated requirements.

Footnote 1 states a 15% limit on direct private-asset investments or exposures under UT Code section 7.3. That separate investment restriction must not be substituted for the 50% aggregate classification threshold, used to cap observed exposure artificially, or treated as permission for all exposures below 50%. Overall investment-limit compliance is outside this question.

Footnote 6 excludes a category of assessed Funds. It does not exclude every listed closed-ended holding from indirect exposure. In particular, the BDC description must not be conflated with the LAF exclusion.

The factors also include home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements or conditions under unit d4148dd852cee.u28.4505. These are not represented as executable factor assessments. Like the listed asset and Fund characteristics, they inform SFC discretion and do not themselves substitute for an actual designation.

The consultation statement is supported as encouragement. Its OBLIGATION/SHOULD metadata would overstate the source if a downstream process treated it as a mandatory consultation condition or an independent classification trigger.

A false classification result does not establish overall compliance, permission to distribute without other requirements, or absence of classification under another regime. OUT_OF_SCOPE for a LAF likewise does not establish that the Fund is non-complex under its separate regime.

The discretionary-factor and definition omissions are upstream assessment boundaries, not automatic instructions to add predicates to the Boolean rule. Their proper treatment depends on whether a separate, adequately supported input-assessment process exists.

additional_concerns: These are proposals about the retained source and declared representation. No executable implementation, Fund-specific evidence or runtime results are supplied. The assessments do not establish an actual Fund classification or authorize pruning any required pair.

Footnote 7 places the holistic discretionary assessment in cases below 50% of NAV. The representation does not explicitly guard its designation branch with that condition. For known consistent Boolean inputs, threshold OR designation equals threshold OR (NOT threshold AND designation). Under the declared uncertainty semantics, they can differ: an unknown threshold and a true designation yield TRUE in the supplied representation, but UNKNOWN with an added below-threshold guard. The packet does not establish that re-testing the current threshold is necessary to rely on an actual applicable designation; adding the guard is therefore not an established repair.

The automatic route requires total direct and indirect exposure of 50% or more, including exactly 50%. It does not require a separate SFC designation. Discretionary factors, whether individually or collectively present, must not be converted into an automatic designation rule.

The runtime states: 'A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch.' A designation conflict can therefore block a known threshold result, and an irrelevant conflict may block scope handling. This is an additional evidentiary restriction not stated in the circular. Whether it is an intended operational safeguard remains unresolved.

Exposure measurement, look-through, valuation, netting and aggregation are not implemented or resolved by the supplied source. Any additional authority needed to resolve them is missing and unidentified. A broad input description is not evidence that upstream exposure calculations faithfully implement the circular.

Reliance on designation requires the actual Fund-specific SFC decision and evidence of temporal applicability. Neither is supplied. An unsearched designation history cannot establish a false input. Missing holdings, measurement or designation evidence must remain unknown rather than be treated as evidence of absence.

The supplied source does not establish the circular's effective date, designation persistence or applicable subsequent amendments. Its statement that examples may be updated does not establish that an update exists. Assessment-time applicability remains unresolved where material.

All three supplied external dependencies have null source_hash values and no descriptions identifying their authorities. None qualifies as AVAILABLE, and no particular missing authority can reliably be mapped to those IDs. Pair-level NONE_DECLARED assessments concern the narrow source-supported claims, not completeness of the evidence needed for a Fund-specific application.

External authorities referenced but not supplied with identifiable dependency mappings include UT Code section 7.3; the LAF circular refNo=25EC9; Code of Conduct paragraph 5.5; Chapter 6 of the Guidelines on Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms and relevant FAQs; the internal product-approval circular refNo=16EC11; and the Advertising Guidelines Applicable to Collective Investment Schemes Authorized under the Product Codes. Their full requirements remain unchecked. The circular's source-attributed BDC description does not independently verify the US Investment Company Act of 1940.

Footnote 1 states a separate 15% investment limit for direct private-asset investments or exposures. That limit must not replace the 50% aggregate classification threshold, artificially cap observed exposures, or imply permission for exposures below 50%. Investment-limit compliance is outside the typed question.

The LAF exclusion concerns the assessed Fund, not every listed closed-ended holding in its portfolio. The BDC description must not be conflated with the exclusion or used to remove BDC-related indirect exposure from aggregation.

The non-exhaustive designation factors also include home-regulator distribution restrictions, requirements or conditions in unit d4148dd852cee.u28.4505. They are not executed by the formula. If a separate factor assessment is undertaken, any applicable home-regulator instruments would need to be supplied; their existence, content and dependency mapping are unresolved.

The consultation statement is encouragement. Its OBLIGATION/SHOULD metadata would overstate the source if used to impose mandatory consultation, suspend the automatic threshold pending consultation, or create another classification trigger.

A FALSE result addresses only the two circular-based classification routes within established scope. It establishes neither overall compliance nor permission to distribute without other requirements. OUT_OF_SCOPE for a LAF likewise does not determine its treatment under the separate LAF regime.

OMITS for definitions, exposure interpretation and discretionary factors identifies the boundary of the executable representation. It does not by itself require adding predicates to the formula. An adequately supported upstream assessment could be sufficient; whether such an assessment exists is unresolved.

additional_concerns: Candidate node.ad3ed6f7c586444ec7213491 introduces an unsupported positive-NAV legal-scope condition. With otherwise established scope and an applicable SFC designation, unknown NAV produces UNKNOWN and nonpositive NAV produces OUT_OF_SCOPE. The source supplies no such restriction on the designation route. A measurement-validity check and a legal-scope exclusion have different consequences.

The arithmetic in node.ad3ed6f7c586444ec7213491 expresses twice the aggregate exposure being at least NAV. It preserves the inclusive half-NAV boundary for suitable exact, commensurate inputs; this does not verify the upstream valuation method, look-through treatment, overlap handling or numeric implementation.

Footnote 7 expressly situates holistic designation assessment below 50%. Both candidates may consume an actual applicable designation without independently recreating that assessment, but neither establishes the validity of the designation process or authorizes a manager to substitute its own factor assessment for an SFC decision.

The packet contains no exposure methodology, Fund-specific designation decision, assessment date, or rules governing persistence after threshold changes. These gaps do not invalidate the circular's stated routes, but they limit any Fund-specific determination.

The labels OMITS for exposure definitions and designation factors identify unimplemented upstream assessments. They do not establish that the classification formulas require instrument-level or regulator-decision logic, and they do not authorize pruning those source claims.

The three supplied external dependency IDs have null source_hash values and no authority-name mappings. None qualifies as AVAILABLE, and assigning any of them to UT Code paragraph 7.3 or footnote 8 authorities would invent a catalogue match.

If a Fund's LAF category is disputed, the LAF circular identified in footnote 6 may be needed. It is not supplied or mapped to a dependency ID. Its absence does not undermine the express exclusion, and exclusion from this circular does not establish exemption under other rules.

Claim claim.e97a5ab05dba08850901077d faithfully says consultation is encouraged. Its OBLIGATION/SHOULD metadata could nevertheless be read more strongly than the source; neither mandatory consultation nor automatic classification pending consultation is supported.

The global CONFLICT blocking rule is a declared evidence-handling policy, not a classification condition established by the circular. It can prevent a Boolean result despite another independently sufficient route; that operational consequence should remain distinct from a substantive finding that classification is not required.

Neither a FALSE classification result nor OUT_OF_SCOPE establishes compliance with the separate 15% investment limit, sale requirements, disclosure duties or other applicable rules. The candidate questions appropriately limit their negative-result meanings.

PRESERVES findings concern the stated classification relationship using supplied judgment facts. The representation does not establish LAF status, measure aggregate exposure, perform holistic assessment or prove an operative designation. The OMITS findings for channel identification and home-regulator factors identify this delegated work, not established Boolean defects.

The authority dispute for the general designation power admits two scopes: the circular suffices to establish the claim, while applying the route requires missing fund-specific decision evidence. NONE_DECLARED is proposed for the former; MISSING remains appropriate if the assessed dependency is the particular operative decision. No decision is inferred from the absence of supplied evidence.

The authority dispute for home-regulator conditions similarly separates a supported general factor list from an unresolved application inquiry. No extra authority is needed for the list; which home-regulator instruments, if any, are necessary for a particular assessment remains uncertain.

The runtime states: "A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch." This can block classification despite an independently established threshold route, or block OUT_OF_SCOPE despite established LAF status. It is an additional evidence-handling policy, not a restriction imposed by the circular; it must not be presented as a substantive classification exception.

The unrestricted designation disjunct does not alter an ordinary Boolean classification outcome at or above 50%, because the threshold independently suffices. It nevertheless does not encode footnote 7's restriction on the described holistic assessment and cannot establish the discretionary power's scope above the threshold.

Named intermediaries, a home-regulator restriction, enhanced scrutiny, missing disclosure, or breach of the 15% investment limit do not independently establish an SFC designation. The representation supplies no such extra route. Nor does it create an existing-fund exemption or an update-related classification grace period.

The packet does not establish measurement dates, valuation, look-through, netting, aggregation, designation duration or classification persistence after exposure falls below 50%. The temporal input convention does not resolve those issues. FALSE means only that both retained routes are established absent on the stated assessment basis; OUT_OF_SCOPE does not mean non-complex under another regime.

The three supplied external dependency IDs have null source_hash values and no descriptions identifying the authorities they represent. None supports AVAILABLE, and none can safely be assigned to a missing authority. Empty dependency_ids preserve this unresolved mapping.

PRESERVES findings concern the stated classification relationship using supplied judgment facts. The representation does not establish LAF status, measure aggregate exposure, perform holistic assessment or prove an operative designation. The OMITS findings for channel identification and home-regulator factors identify this delegated work, not established Boolean defects.

The authority dispute for the general designation power admits two scopes: the circular suffices to establish the claim, while applying the route requires missing fund-specific decision evidence. NONE_DECLARED is proposed for the former; MISSING remains appropriate if the assessed dependency is the particular operative decision. No decision is inferred from the absence of supplied evidence.

The authority dispute for home-regulator conditions similarly separates a supported general factor list from an unresolved application inquiry. No extra authority is needed for the list; which home-regulator instruments, if any, are necessary for a particular assessment remains uncertain.

The runtime states: "A conflicting fact anywhere in the rule dependency closure blocks evaluation with CONFLICT even on an unselected branch." This can block classification despite an independently established threshold route, or block OUT_OF_SCOPE despite established LAF status. It is an additional evidence-handling policy, not a restriction imposed by the circular; it must not be presented as a substantive classification exception.

The unrestricted designation disjunct does not alter an ordinary Boolean classification outcome at or above 50%, because the threshold independently suffices. It nevertheless does not encode footnote 7's restriction on the described holistic assessment and cannot establish the discretionary power's scope above the threshold.

Named intermediaries, a home-regulator restriction, enhanced scrutiny, missing disclosure, or breach of the 15% investment limit do not independently establish an SFC designation. The representation supplies no such extra route. Nor does it create an existing-fund exemption or an update-related classification grace period.

The packet does not establish measurement dates, valuation, look-through, netting, aggregation, designation duration or classification persistence after exposure falls below 50%. The temporal input convention does not resolve those issues. FALSE means only that both retained routes are established absent on the stated assessment basis; OUT_OF_SCOPE does not mean non-complex under another regime.

The three supplied external dependency IDs have null source_hash values and no descriptions identifying the authorities they represent. None supports AVAILABLE, and none can safely be assigned to a missing authority. Empty dependency_ids preserve this unresolved mapping.

The suitability claim is supported as the circular's summary, with incorporated scope reserved. Reading its actor label as an unconditional duty on every possible seller would exceed what is established here; missing incorporated qualifications are not evidence of a defect in this classification formula.

additional_concerns: Exposure measurement, LAF identification and operative designation are supplied judgments. The formula does not establish their factual or legal correctness. OMITS findings for upstream assessments do not alone establish a defect in the scoped classification formula.

Footnote 7 limits the holistic designation assessment to exposure below 50% of NAV. The OR preserves the outcome when the automatic threshold is met, but does not implement this procedural qualification or establish designation persistence.

The global conflict-blocking rule adds an evidentiary restriction not stated in the circular: conflict on an otherwise unnecessary branch can block an independently established route. CONFLICT must not be interpreted as absence of classification.

FALSE requires both retained routes to be established absent for an in-scope Fund. It does not establish non-complex status under other regimes, declassification following reduced exposure, or permission to sell.
The three missing dependency IDs have no supplied authority-name mapping. None can reliably be assigned to a named missing authority.

Other absent authorities include the LAF circular 25EC9, UT Code section 7.3, Internal Product Approval Process circular 16EC11 and the referenced Advertising Guidelines. They concern separate regimes or obligations; their absence does not itself defeat the retained classification predicate.

For the open-ended examples claim, the circular supplies all authority necessary to establish the stated proposition. Whether subsequent SFC updates are needed for a particular assessment occasion remains unresolved; this separate uncertainty is retained in the follow-up.
